subject: Dedicated reservation options and GPU onramp for Polaris Biotech
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@polarisbio.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — throughput profile and timeline

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. We sketched internal numbers and realized we need clarity on a few things before the procurement team will move: expected minimum GPU floor, how ramp scheduling looks over a quarter, and fallbacks if we exceed commit during spikes.

I've attached a simple demand forecast (weekly inference minutes + p95 latency requirement) — can you propose 2–3 reservation structures with clear activation windows and what warm capacity looks like?

We're targeting production in Q4 and want the pricing/activation table to feed our procurement RFx next week.

Best,
Alex
Head of ML Ops, Polaris Biotech

Attachment: polaris_demand_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@polarisbio.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-26T13:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — throughput profile and timeline

Alex —

Appreciate the forecast. Attached is a short proposal (PDF) with three opinionated reservation options and what each means for latency, burstability, and billing cadence. High level:

- Option A (Conservative anchor): 40 min GPUs steady; burst pool + hot standby for 20% spikes; activation window 30 days; best for predictable, lower-cost run-to-production.
- Option B (Phased onramp): start at 16 min GPUs month 1, scale to 32 month 2, 48 month 3 with automated warm-up windows; includes a 2-week pre-warm for critical launches.
- Option C (Throughput-first): 80 min GPUs with aggressive warm cache and KV persistence for high qps; cheapest per-token at scale but higher commit.

I've included an appendix with expected token cost delta per option and the SLA differences. Karthik and Lauren, flagged some infra concerns inline — anything to add on sizing assumptions?

Next step: tell me which option you'd like a formal SOW/term sheet for and we'll lock lead times and credits.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_reservation_options_v3.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-27T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — throughput profile and timeline

Ben —

Quick notes on the appendix (technical sizing):

- The forecast assumes median sequence length of 512 tokens; if Polaris shifts to longer context (1k+), Option B's month-2 step will underprovision cache memory and KV eviction will drive latency. Recommend adding a staged quantization profile for Option B to keep cost bounded.
- Warm-up: suggest a rolling pre-warm (30% of cluster warmed each day over the 2-week window) rather than a single bulk warm to avoid token-price shock.
- Burst pool: implement cross-region fallback to our secondary pool (us-west) with model variant rollback to a smaller quantized model — call this fallback path in the SLO table.

I'll draft a small paragraph to insert about the rolling warm strategy if you want.

-Karthik
Senior Infra PM, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-06-29T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — throughput profile and timeline

Alex / Samira —

Thanks for the fast turnaround on the forecast. Per Karthik's notes, we've updated Option B to include:

- Staged quantization profile (FP16 -> 4-bit per workload phase).
- Rolling pre-warm schedule: 30% cluster warm/day over 14 days.
- Explicit fallback: cross-region secondary pool + auto-rollback to quantized variant (listed in SLO table).

Practical ask for procurement: which of the three financial profiles do you want to see in the RFx tables? We can publish a straight monthly commit price, or a blended commit + burst price that limits overage to a capped multiplier. My recommendation for Polaris' forecast is Option B (Phased onramp) with the blended commit/burst profile — it keeps cost upside limited while giving you runway.

If that sounds good I'll prepare a term sheet and SOW (3–6 months activation milestones) by Friday.

Best,
Ben
